title: Lavender Tallow Balm: My Weirdly Effective Nighttime Thing
body:
Okay so it's like 10:42 PM. My phone's at 12%. I just washed my face with that cheap drugstore cleanser, the green one that smells like chemicals and mint. My skin feels tight. You know that feeling. Like a drum. Not good. The air in here is weirdly dry for spring, the heat's still kicking on sometimes, and my face is just not having it. Red patches near my nose. That one spot on my forehead that's always flaky. I'm staring at this little jar on my sink. The Whipped Tallow Balm. Lavender. It sounds like something a pioneer would use. Or a candle. Beef fat on my face. I was so skeptical when it showed up. But here I am, about to use it again. Because my skin has been... chill. Calm. I don't know how else to say it.

My tallow balm routine started out of pure desperation. It was late March, but winter had left my hands looking like a cracked desert landscape. My elbows were a whole other story. I tried everything. Lotions that felt like slick plastic. Creams that sat on top and did nothing. Expensive stuff from fancy stores that made my wallet cry and my skin just shrug. Then I kept seeing this beef tallow skincare stuff. Grass-fed, whipped, all that. Mimics your skin's own oil. Sounded like hippie nonsense, honestly. But I was at the point where I'd try anything. Found this little shop on Etsy. French-made. Ordered it one night while half-watching a baking show. Forgot about it until it arrived.

## How I Actually Use This Stuff

So the jar is small. Cute. I unscrew it. The texture is... not what you'd expect. It's not greasy like lard. It's whipped. Like if butter and thick cream had a baby. Kind of waxy at first? But then it warms up between your fingers. You need the tiniest amount. A scoop about the size of a pea. Seriously. Any more and you'll feel like you've dipped your face in a frying pan. I rub it between my palms to melt it a bit.

Then I just... pat it on. Mostly at night. My how to use tallow balm method is not scientific. I focus on the dry zones. Cheeks. Forehead. The sides of my nose that get angry. Sometimes I'll smooth whatever's left on my hands over my neck. It goes on feeling rich. Not heavy, but present. You feel it. For a minute, you look shiny. Like you've been sweating. I usually brush my teeth after to give it a second to sink in. By the time I'm done, that shine is gone. It just... goes in. My skin feels soft. Not slippery soft. More like... hydrated? Protected? I don't have a good word for it.

Oh, and the smell. The lavender. It's not that fake, sweet candle smell. It's more... herbal. Like crushed plants. Green. A little earthy. It's strong when you open the jar but fades fast once it's on your skin. My partner said it smells like a clean barn. Which sounds bad but isn't? It's relaxing. It smells like sleep. I put it on and my brain gets the signal that it's time to shut down. I think that's the point.

## Why This Beef Tallow Thing Makes Any Sense

I had to look this up because I was putting cow fat on my face and felt I should have a reason. So tallow, from grass-fed cows, is apparently really similar to the oils our own skin makes. Our sebum. So it absorbs deep instead of sitting on top like a silicone coat. It's got vitamins A, D, E, K. All that good stuff. For skin that's sensitive, or wrecked from winter, or dealing with eczema patches... it makes a kind of sense. It's not stripping anything. It's giving your skin something it already knows how to use.

My daily skincare with tallow is stupid simple now. Morning, I just splash with water. Maybe a tiny, tiny bit of the balm on any super dry spots if I'm staying home. Night is the main event. Cleanse. Pat dry. Tallow balm. Done. I've stopped using like five other products. A serum. A night cream. An oil. This one jar replaced them. Which is weird to say. I didn't expect it to work like that.

This is a tangent but my bathroom sink is way less cluttered now. Just the cleanser, this jar, and my toothpaste. It's kind of nice. Less to think about. My skin seems to like the simplicity too. It's not being bombarded with ten different actives.

## What My Skin Is Doing Now

Okay so the results. I've been using this for... six weeks? Maybe two months. I'm bad with time. I'm on my second jar now, which says something because I never finish skincare products.

The flaky patch on my forehead is just gone. Not hiding. Gone. The redness around my nose is way down. It's not perfect, but it's not an angry beacon anymore. My skin just feels... even. Balanced is a word people use, I guess. It doesn't freak out as much. If I get a weird stress pimple, it heals faster and doesn't leave a red mark for weeks. The biggest thing is in the morning. My face doesn't feel tight. It feels normal. Like skin. Not like parchment paper.

My hands were the real test. I used the balm on them at night too, with cotton gloves. The cracks are healed. They're not baby-soft or whatever, but they're not painful. They're functional hands again. I got a jar for my mom because her knuckles get so bad in the cold. She texted me last week saying "what is this magic butter." So there's that.

I got mine from this Etsy shop, Petite Ferme or something like that. The jar is simple. No crazy packaging. It feels honest. I like that.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Weirdly, yeah. For me it is. The science-y reason is it's close to our skin's own oils, so it sinks in and helps repair the barrier instead of just coating it. My face seems to recognize it as food, not an intruder.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
I was terrified of this. I have combo skin that can get clogged. But this hasn't broken me out. At all. I think because it absorbs properly, it doesn't just sit in your pores like some heavy creams do. Start with a tiny amount though. Less is more.

**What does the lavender tallow balm smell like?**
Not like a cheap air freshener. It's a real, herbal lavender smell. Earthy. A little green. It's strong in the jar but once you rub it in, it mellows out fast into this gentle, calming scent that just makes you want to go to bed.

So yeah. That's my weird little jar of cow fat. I didn't think I'd be the person recommending tallow balm to anyone, but here I am. If your skin is being difficult, feeling tight or angry or just off, and the usual stuff isn't cutting it... might be worth a shot. It's become this non-negotiable part of my night now. Wash face. Tallow. Done. My skin's happy. I'm happy. And I'm definitely ordering another one soon.
